key_insight: Finite-energy bosonic codes let a single oscillator sense an external force while protecting an unknown logical qubit, with probe readout independent of the logical state under continuous photon loss.
engineering_relevance: The approach could combine force sensing and recoverable quantum memory in one superconducting oscillator, with encoding choices guided by hardware noise and nonlinearities.
method: Encode logical amplitudes across discrete wave-packet sites and the force signal in a shared internal coordinate.
Use binomial site recovery to correct logical errors and cancel packet-dependent probe distortions.
Read out the force probe at the endpoint without dependence on the stored logical state.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports memory infidelity of O(γ^(r+1)) and residual memory–probe correlations of O(γ^(r+2)) for a (2r+2)-packet code, plus superconducting-circuit benchmarks including photon-number dephasing and Kerr nonlinearity.
watch_item: Hardware performance depends on competing dephasing and Kerr effects; the abstract reports benchmarks rather than an experimental demonstration.
paper_title: Force Sensing in a Recoverable Bosonic Quantum Memory
